title: Mastering Breastfeeding and Early Physical Care
summary: Breastfeeding is not just nutrition — it is the emotional and immune lifeline after birth. The first drops of colostrum are rich in antibodies and are the newborn's first natural vaccination. Successful breastfeeding depends on a deep latch on the nipple and areola to avoid pain and cracking, and on responding to early hunger cues (mouth movements, sucking on hands) before the baby reaches the crying stage. The father's role here is central: caring for the mother and providing her with rest, water and food so she can devote herself to breastfeeding.
try_this: This week: practise comfortable breastfeeding positions (the cradle hold or lying on your side), and make sure of skin-to-skin contact straight after birth and during feeds. The father takes on burping and nappy changes after each feed to lighten the mother's load.
reflection_prompts: What challenges do you anticipate with breastfeeding, and how can your partner assist?
How can you recognize your newborn's subtle hunger cues before crying begins?
